header.name: Setting up Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in India
offered_to:
1. B.Tech Pre-final Year students
2. B.Tech Final year students
3. Pre-Final year M.Tech students
(UG/PG)
header.description: India has become a global hub for Global Capability Centres (GCCs), hosting over 1,500 centres employing 1.6 million+ professionals. A course on setting up GCCs is vital to equip individuals with knowledge of regulatory frameworks, FDI norms, SEZ policies, and operational strategies essential for launching and scaling such centres. With GCCs evolving into innovation hubs focusing on AI, analytics, and cybersecurity, this course can help align talent and infrastructure to industry needs. The course also promotes interdisciplinary learning across business, law, tech, and policy, fostering academic research and strategic collaboration. As global competition intensifies, such a course enhances India’s attractiveness for future GCC investments, supports regional development, and creates a talent pipeline geared towards high-value global roles—making it a timely and strategic offering for academia and industry alike.

lecture_topics: Introduction to GCCs: Definitions, scope, history
India as a GCC hub: Macro trends, policy support, and FDI landscape
GCC business case: Cost-benefit analysis and value creation models
Legal & regulatory aspects: SEZs, STPI, IP, labour laws
Organization design & operating models (COEs, shared services)
Risk management: Operational, geopolitical, compliance risks
Talent strategy: Hiring, training, and retention in GCCs
Transition management: Planning, knowledge transfer, go-live, Hyper care
Change management & culture alignment in global teams
Innovation and value creation through GCCs
Guest session/Case study from industry leader

assessments.type_label: Final Project: End-to-End GCC Setup Plan
